claims.text: The X-CAL intercalibration tables that put each microwave sensor on GMI's scale are delivered by the GPM Intercalibration (X-CAL) Working Group, led by Rachael Kroodsma at NASA GSFC (Code 615); the L1C ATBD names the working group, not a person, and the only GSICS-hosted copy of the tables is Wes Berg's (CSU) V05 set dated 11 Dec 2018. No funding source is published.

evidence.passage: Dr. Rachael A. Kroodsma is a Research Physical Scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center with the Advanced Instruments and Measurement Systems branch (Code 615). … She leads the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) inter-calibration working group (XCAL) … The Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Intercalibration Working Group (XCAL) is responsible for delivering the intercalibration tables for the GPM constellation microwave radiometers to create the Level 1C dataset. The XCAL team works on developing intercalibration techniques and monitoring the calibration/stability of the current sensors in the constellation to ensure a quality precipitation product.
evidence.location: bio paragraph; Current Projects: GPM XCAL (txt lines 37, 49-53)

evidence.passage: The GPM GMI brightness temperatures have been defined as the calibration reference for the GPM constellation. As a result, no changes were made to the GMI brightness temperature (Tb). … 1C.GPM.GMI.XCAL2016-C.tbl Intercalibration Tb offset table … 1C.DMSP-F16.SSMIS.XCAL2021-V.tbl … 1C.GCOMW1.AMSR2.XCAL2016-V.tbl … 1C.NOAA-NOAA20.ATMS.XCAL2019-V.tbl … 1C.NOAA-NOAA21.ATMS.XCAL2023-V.tbl … 1C.METOP-B.MHS.XCAL2016-V.tbl Intercalibration Tb offset table for METOP-B | 1C.METOP-C.MHS.XCAL2019-V.tbl Intercalibration Tb offset table for METOP-C … 1C.WSFM1.MWI.XCAL2026-V.tbl Intercalibration Tb offset table for WSFM1 … 1C.GOSATGW.AMSR3.XCAL2026-V.tbl Intercalibration Tb offset table

GSICS Wiki>Development web>Microwave-Deliverable (16 Jan 2019, ManikBali) … by Wes Berg (Colorado State University … ) … The attached tar file provided by Web Berg contains the current Level 1C intercalibration tables for 13 imagers and 11 sounders along with a couple of journal pubs, software to read and apply the tables … Description: PMM XCAL Intercalibration tables for Level 1C data (V05) … Reference Sensor: GPM GMI Version V05 … Date: 11 December 2018 … Contact: Wesley Berg (berg@atmos.colostate.edu)

claims.confidence_reason: PPS's own ATBD files, read as raw text.
claims.sole_source_reason: PPS's own ATBD is the authority for its own document version.

claims.text: The Late Run's gauge calibration is a set of climatological coefficients computed once from the reprocessed V07B Final Run (in use from 1 June 2024); the Aug 2026 ATBD still names GPCC V2022 and no NASA document says the coefficients were updated or frozen after the Final record ended on 2025-09-30. GPCC V2025 (merging Full Data and Monitoring) has been out since March 2026, but nothing found says it reaches IMERG; by the ATBD's design it would reach the Late Run only through a new Final Run (V08) and new climatological coefficients.

evidence.passage: The baseline is for the Early and Late half-hour land estimates to be calibrated to the Final Run with climatological coefficients that vary by month and location

When a new version of IMERG is released, retrospective processing the Early and Late Runs is carried out after reprocessing the Final Run to allow computation of climatological coefficients that calibrate Early and Late to the Final monthly product (which has gauge information).
We use two GPCC products: the V2022 Full Data Analysis

Following these actions, climatological calibrations were computed for the Early and Late Runs to the Final Run, and both Initial Processing (IP) and RP for the Early and Late Runs began on 3 June 2024, with IP taking effect starting 1 June. … Applied climatological adjustment to the Early and Late Runs based on the Final Run. … This ensures more consistency in the bias characteristics among the Early, Late, and Final Runs.

The GPCC creates multiple products, and two are used in IMERG. The Full Data Reanalysis (currently Version 2022) is a retrospective analysis that covers the period 1891-2020, and it is used in IMERG for the span <1998> 2000-2020. Thereafter we use the GPCC Monitoring Product (currently Version 2022) … When the GPCC analyses are updated, we switch to the new version and continue processing forward, even though (in principle) there is a small inhomogeneity as a result.

GPCC Precipitation Analysis Monthly Version 2025 (at 0.25°, 0.5°, 1.0°, 2.5°) … It merges the former Full Data Monthly with the Monitoring Product. … January 1891 - present month … the data set is continuously extended by the latest month with a latency of two months. … It is foreseen to update the GPCC Precipitation Analysis Monthly with a cycle of three to four years.
We offer a new version, V2025, of the GPCC Product of monthly global land-surface precipitation which is now a combination of analysis and monitoring product and the successor of V2022.

For the Late and Early Runs, the V07 production will continue as the parent products are being upgraded to V08. … Starting March 1, the CORRA calibration has been set to climatological values that are periodically updated to reflect seasonal conditions. That is, the calibration of GPROF V08 to CORRA V07 is being computed from selected seasonal periods in previous years, then used for the same time period in 2026. The Late and Early Runs will be in this “hybrid V07” posture until the near-real-time processing system is ready to switch to V08, which is expected to take place no sooner than fall of 2026.

claims.applicability: Inference about how V2025 would reach the Late Run rests on the ATBD's description of the method, not on a NASA statement.
claims.confidence_reason: NASA documents agree on the method; the absence of an update is an absence of evidence.

claims.text: No IMERG, L1C or GPROF document read names a backup calibration reference if GMI or DPR stopped: GMI is the fixed reference (TMI held that role in the TRMM era), the system runs on the then-current calibration files through dropouts, and a drifting GMI 'cannot be accommodated'; changing that 'would require a major development effort'.

evidence.passage: in the GPM era is carried out as GMI calibrated to CORRA-G. … [Recall that the TMI and GMI products are used as calibrators for all the other satellite precipitation estimates. … ] TMI is reduced to the status of being just another high-quality sensor during the period in which GMI is acting as the calibrator, and vice-versa. … without significant loss of skill it can run with the then-current calibration files, as long as the dropouts do not become too severe. … extended dropouts are rare for the GMI and DPR (and so CORRA-G) … However, using climatological GMI-to-other-PMW calibrations means a drifting GMI cannot be accommodated. … such a modification would require a major development effort.
The GPM GMI brightness temperatures have been defined as the calibration reference for the GPM constellation. As a result, no changes were made to the GMI brightness temperature (Tb).

claims.applicability: DIRS-1/DIRS-5: supports a single-reference dependency inside NASA's own mission.
claims.confidence_reason: Direct statements in the ATBDs; the GPROF V08 ATBD was not found.

This issue persists in both V08A and V08B versions, including the V08B release in which the 'precipitationYesNoFlag' variable was corrected. … We will erase all existing V08A and V08B METOPC data and reprocess all METOPC GPROF data back to its mission start date. … PPS has also stopped processing the current incoming production METOPC data until the new algorithm is installed.  NRT continues its processing METOPC GPROF data.
